title: Golden Gate Bridge
address: Golden Gate Brg, San Francisco, CA 94130
note: the first place i take anyone visiting. walk the east side path from the welcome center and the fog usually shows up on schedule.

title: Ferry Building
note: saturday farmers market is the honest version of this city. go early, get a blue bottle, walk the pier behind it.

title: Golden Gate Park
note: bigger than central park and twice as usable. buffalo paddock, the botanical garden, disc golf, all of it free.

title: Oracle Park
address: 24 Willie Mays Plaza, San Francisco, CA 94107
note: the view alone sells it. kayakers wait in mccovey cove for home runs, which tells you the wind direction is a real factor.

title: Chase Center
note: warriors home floor. take the T, parking is a tax on bad planning.

title: Exploratorium
note: the science museum that treats adults like they still care. the tilted pendulum in the rotunda is worth the walk alone.

title: SFMOMA
venue: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
note: seven floors of it. the living wall on the top floor is the reset button after a long build week.

title: Salesforce Tower
note: the tallest thing downtown and the easiest way to explain where you are to anyone. the crown lights up the sky at night.

title: SoMa startup row
address: South of Market, San Francisco, CA
note: south of market is where the city's startups actually live. hackathon nights, office parties, and the conference crowds that come with them.

title: Mission District
note: valencia street is half coffee shops with laptops and half taquerias. the founder density on a weekday afternoon is the real product.

title: Hayes Valley
note: central, walkable, and full of small shops. a good first neighborhood if you want to live near everything without owning a car.

title: Sunset District
note: foggy, quiet, and half the price of the northeast side. if you want space and a garage, this is where the math starts to work.
